+## #1845 - Remove the remaining committed PR review artifacts
+
+**What was decided.** Remove the review artifact folders for
+[PR #1744](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/1744),
+[PR #1699](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/1699),
+[PR #1710](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/1710) and
+[PR #1724](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/1724).
+Include their readme files and the script that checks the PR #1724 images.
+The xtask guard now checks that these four folders are absent.
+
+Move the PR #1724 evidence out of the current product tree.
+This supersedes the retention decision in the #1122 entry.
+Git history keeps the images, capture provenance and check script.
+The original [capture commit](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/commit/486b03c91c8b1330f1e79ec47500ad68625fdd5a)
+preserves that record. This cleanup does not upload new images.
+
+Remove the optional boundary capture hook. Keep its structural assertions.
+Keep the manual PR #1710 capture test, but write its output to
+`camcraft-review-1710` under the operating system's temporary directory.
+
+**Why.** Issue #1794 removed the precedent for keeping review evidence in
+the product tree. These files are review artifacts, not product inputs.
+PR screenshots belong in PR bodies, with images on the author's fork
+in its images-only branch. The boundary hook accepted an arbitrary path
+and could recreate a removed folder. The manual capture also wrote into
+a removed folder. Its temporary output keeps the capture useful.
+
+**Considered and dropped.** Keep a special exception for PR #1724:
+its evidence remains available in Git history, so it needs no exception.
+Keep the boundary hook with its arbitrary destination: this could recreate
+the folders that the guard rejects. Delete the manual PR #1710 capture:
+changing its output directory is smaller and preserves the capture tool.
+A general ban on documentation images would reject valid product content.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Small. The guard names four additional folders.
+The manual capture destination is one line. Future review evidence can
+use the images-only branch without restoring files to the product tree.

-# PR #1699 UI evidence
-
-Both images render the shipping egui shell through its existing headless
-`egui_kittest` harness at 2400 × 950. The viewport is the harness's flat
-placeholder; these images document the model page and import status, not
-3D rendering. No pixel golden was changed.

-closed shell `#17`, leaving five faces and a missing wall. This is the same
-input used by the structural UI regression test.

-closed shell because it meshes open. The document stays empty. This image

-only `ImportModel::within` to call the previous graded loader. The source
-change was restored after capture.

-# PR #1710: WCS page and viewport evidence
-
-These are review captures, not pixel snapshot goldens. Each image renders the
-shipping WCS page and shell with a GPU-rendered `View3D` texture. No viewport
-placeholder or mockup is used. The corner scene is a 20 × 20 × 40 mm block; the
-centre scene is a 20 mm diameter, 40 mm high cylinder. Box markers are on the
-bottom level so the clicked top corner or top rim centre misses them.
-
-| Target | Before | After |
-|---|---|---|
-| Part corner (20, 20, 40) | ![Corner before](corner-before.png) | ![Corner after](corner-after.png) |
-| Boss rim centre (0, 0, 40) | ![Centre before](centre-before.png) | ![Centre after](centre-after.png) |
-
-Both versions start with WCS origin (1, 2, 3), armed **Pick markers in viewport**,
-and the same camera. Each capture is taken after the same click. Before uses the
-picker behavior and WCS hint from parent `101d82f9`; an unused `queue_vertex`
-helper from the reviewed head remains only so the current test suite compiles.
-The origin stays at (1, 2, 3). After
-uses reviewed head `b3733f46c348f9146747d1d05a1cc91f4099604c`; the origin moves
-to the clicked target. The WCS page readout shows the resulting position.
-
-The ignored test
-`egui_app::tests::review_1710_evidence::review_1710_wcs_page_and_viewport_evidence`
-reproduces the captures. It asserts that the click misses box markers, reaches
-the expected WCS origin, and leaves the WCS controls and armed hint visible.
-It requires a real graphics adapter and fails explicitly without one.
-
-From `crates/ui`, capture the current version with:
-
-```sh
-cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib review_1710_wcs_page_and_viewport_evidence -- --ignored --nocapture
-```
-
-To reproduce the before images in a disposable worktree, save the current
-`crates/ui/src/wcs_circle_pick.rs` and
-`crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs`, replace only those two files with their
-`101d82f9` versions, retaining the unused `queue_vertex` helper in the picker
-so the current tests compile, and run the same command with `PR1710_BEFORE=1`. Restore
-both files byte for byte afterwards. Without that environment flag, the parent
-picker must make the origin assertion fail; restoring the current picker must
-make it pass. The capture test writes only this evidence directory and never
-updates `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/`.
-
-If adding an environment variable prevents adapter discovery in a sandbox,
-create `docs/reviews/1710/.before-capture` instead, run the unmodified capture
-command, then remove that marker. The marker is never committed.

-import pathlib
-import re
-import struct
-import sys
-
-root = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
-readme = (root / "README.md").read_text()
-body = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text() if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None
-for control in ("drill", "bore", "thread"):
-    for state in ("before", "after"):
-        name = f"{control}-{state}.png"
-        for label, text in (("README", readme), ("PR body", body)):
-            if text is not None:
-                assert re.search(r"!\[[^\]]*\]\([^\s)]*" + re.escape(name) + r"\)", text), f"{label} lacks image {name}"
-        data = (root / name).read_bytes()
-        assert data[:8] == b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n", f"invalid PNG: {name}"
-        width, height = struct.unpack(">II", data[16:24])
-        assert width >= 620 and height >= 600, f"unexpected dimensions: {name}"
-print("PASS: all six Drill, Bore and Thread before/after screenshots are embedded")
